history.dynasty: ancient origins (Treta Yuga legend); historical mentions under later Chalukya/Kakatiya and Vijayanagara periods; major reconstruction by the Government of Telangana
history.period: Treta Yuga legend (Skanda Purana mentions); 1148 CE inscriptional reference (king Tribhuvana Malludu, Kolanupaka inscription); 15th-century visit of Krishnadevaraya; massive expansion/rebuild 2016-March 2022
history.summary: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple at Yadagirigutta, also called Yadadri, is Telangana's most famous Vaishnavite shrine - 'Telangana's own Tirupati' - a Pancha Narasimha Kshetram on a hillock ~60 km from Hyderabad. Legend says sage Yadarishi (also rendered Yadava) meditated in a cave here and Vishnu appeared before him in five forms; the cave remains the garbhagriha. Worship follows Pancharatra Agama tradition (Suprabhatam composed by Sri Vangeepuram Narasimhacharyulu). Historical anchors: 1148 CE Kolanupaka inscription referencing king Tribhuvana Malludu's visits, and 15th-century Krishnadevaraya recording his visit before battle. The temple was massively rebuilt and expanded 2016-2022 with black granite, grand gopurams, and a golden Sudarshana Chakra atop the sanctuary. Identity confirmed: this is the famous Yadadri temple.

name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (Yadadri)
town_description: Yadagirigutta is a small temple town in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district of Telangana, built around the Yadadri hillock. It is one of the state's busiest pilgrimage centres, drawing 5,000-8,000 devotees daily, and is well connected to Hyderabad (~60 km) and the nearby Bhongir fort.
